books.title: Anamorphic on a Budget
books.tagline: Start shooting anamorphic without breaking the bank!
description: The improved version of the Anamorphic on a Budget guide I have at my blog!

When I wrote this guide as my graduation project in 2013, I didn't expect translating it to English. Five years after the unexpected translation and a lot of research later, I decided to revisit my original work.

This revised edition features updated key concepts, higher resolution images and an expanded section on post-production aimed not only at MagicLantern users - plus the minor bug fixes of grammar and vocabulary!

books.title: Anamorfake It
books.fullTitle: Anamorfake It Until You Make It!
books.tagline: Achieve the anamorphic lens look on the cheap!
description: From the creator of Anamorphic on a Budget comes a new guide. One that doesn't involve anamorphic at all!

The goal of Anamorfake It Until You Make It is to create the anamorphic look minus the nuisances and expenses of anamorphic adapters (and, oh boy, these are expensive right now). This guide is focused on shooting spherical, keeping it cheap and delivering a look that not even pros can tell you're faking.
This is a guide with plenty of techniques using gear and tools you are likely to own - or that costs next to nothing!

books.title: USSR Lens Buyer's Guide
books.tagline: Dive into classic Soviet lenses for a vintage look among today's clinical optics.
description: Soviet lenses have always been a popular and affordable option to get into vintage glass. But which ones to choose?

In this guide I'll take you through a variety of Soviet glass, focusing on the super-adaptable M42 mount which can be used on pretty much any modern camera (DSLR or mirrorless), in a way that helps you identify the lenses you like and provide an easy way to acquire them.

You will also understand Soviet lens naming conventions, learn a few online myths about them, find tutorials and recommendations for disassembly and servicing, read about extremely rare optics and the modern take on well-established optics.
